The must-sees

11 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Bridge

    Bridge of Sighs

    It was built around 1600 to take prisoners from the courts to the new prisons across the canal. The romantic name came later, from 19th-century writers.

    Look for

    Look at the small windows barred with stone. Inside, a wall splits the bridge into two passages, so prisoners going in and out never met.

  2. 02
    Neighbourhood

    Burano

    Burano is known for its needle lace, made here for centuries. Lacemaking is still shown in the island’s Lace Museum.

  3. 03
    Palace

    Doge’s Palace

    For centuries the doge lived here and the republic’s councils met in its painted halls. Tintoretto’s Paradise in the Great Council Hall is among the largest oil paintings in the world.

    Look for

    Look for the lion’s mouths in the walls: stone slots where citizens posted anonymous accusations to the state.

  4. 04
    Museum

    Gallerie dell’Accademia

    It holds works by Bellini, Giorgione, Titian, Tintoretto and Veronese. Leonardo’s Vitruvian Man drawing belongs to the collection but is rarely shown to protect it from light.

    Look for

    Find Giorgione’s Tempest: a soldier, a nursing mother and a lightning bolt, a picture nobody has ever fully explained.

  5. 05
    Neighbourhood

    Murano

    In 1291 the republic moved the glass furnaces here, partly to protect the city from fire. The Glass Museum traces the craft from Roman times.

    Look for

    In the church of Santi Maria e Donato, behind the altar hang large bones said to be from a dragon slain by Saint Donatus.

  6. 06
    Bridge · 1591

    Rialto Bridge

    Antonio da Ponte finished it in 1591, replacing a series of wooden bridges. For nearly three centuries it was the only way to cross the Grand Canal on foot.

    Look for

    On the side of the arch, find the Annunciation in relief: the angel Gabriel on one end and the Virgin Mary on the other.

  7. 07
    Church

    San Giorgio Maggiore

    Andrea Palladio designed the church in the 1560s for the Benedictine monastery here. Its bell tower has a lift and a view straight back across the basin to the piazza.

    Look for

    The façade is two classical temple fronts laid over each other: a tall one for the nave, a wide low one for the aisles.

  8. 08
    Church · 1687

    Santa Maria della Salute

    Venice vowed to build it after the plague of 1630, and Baldassare Longhena spent much of his life on it. Each November a temporary bridge of boats crosses the canal for the feast of the Salute.

    Look for

    Around the dome, giant stone scrolls lean against the drum, which Venetians call the ears.

  9. 09
    Church

    St. Mark’s Basilica

    It was built to hold the relics of St Mark, smuggled out of Alexandria by Venetian merchants in 828. The bronze horses over the door are copies; the originals, taken from Constantinople in 1204, are inside.

    Look for

    At the corner by the Doge’s Palace, four porphyry emperors embrace, looted from Constantinople in 1204. One missing foot was found in Istanbul and is kept there.

  10. 10
    Viewpoint · 1912

    St. Mark’s Campanile

    The old tower collapsed on its own in 1902, killing no one but the caretaker’s cat. It was rebuilt as it had been and reopened in 1912.

    Look for

    At its foot, Sansovino’s small marble Loggetta was pieced back together from fragments found in the rubble of 1902.

  11. 11
    Square

    St. Mark’s Square

    Every other square in the city is a campo, a field. At high tide the piazza is one of the first places to flood, and raised walkways appear across it.

    Look for

    On top of the clock tower, two bronze figures known as the Moors strike the hours on a great bell.
